name: Fourier large spectrum, Chang's lemma and Bohr sets applied to the {0,1} subset-sum distribution
description: For weights a_1..a_n, the characteristic function of the uniform {0,1} subset sum is mu_hat(theta)=prod_i (1+e(a_i theta))/2 with |mu_hat(theta)| = prod_i |cos(pi a_i theta)| <= exp(-2 sum_i ||a_i theta||^2) (||.|| distance to nearest integer). The number of ordered pairs (S,T) of subsets with equal sum equals 2^{2n} * integral over the circle of prod_i cos^2(pi a_i theta), an L^2 Fourier mass of mu_hat; higher moments L^4, L^k count additive quadruples/k-tuples of subset sums. The large spectrum {theta : |mu_hat(theta)| >= rho} is therefore a Bohr-type set {theta : sum ||a_i theta||^2 <= log(1/rho)/2}; Chang's lemma bounds the dimension of a dissociated subset of the large spectrum of a dense set, and Bohr-set machinery (Bogolyubov-Ruzsa, Sanders) converts large spectrum into structure. The 2026 paper arXiv:2609.26619 (Burgin-Mao) concerns sets with small Fourier L^1 (Wiener) norm and is only tangentially related.
authors_year_venue: [uncertain] Method: M.-C. Chang, 'A polynomial bound in Freiman's theorem', Duke Math. J. 113 (2002); T. Sanders, Bohr-set work on Roth/Bogolyubov-Ruzsa (2010-2012); Tao-Vu, Additive Combinatorics (CUP 2006) ch. 4; I. Halasz (1977); Steinerberger, IJNT 19 (2023) 1783-1800 (Fourier proof of the distinct subset sums bound, cited by Costa-Della Fiore). 2026 paper: A. Burgin and J. Mao, 'Remarks on the geometry of sets in Z^d with small Fourier L^1 norm', arXiv:2609.26619v1 (22 Sep 2026), math.NT.
status_and_verification: [uncertain] Method statements are recall (Chang's lemma, Bohr sets) and my own short derivations (the cosine product bound and the collision identity, both elementary and verified by hand). 2609.26619: abstract, table of contents and introduction read via alphaXiv; theorems 6, 10, 11 and proofs NOT read. Steinerberger and Chang not read.
key_theorem_or_bound: [uncertain] Verified by derivation: (1) #{(S,T) subset [n]^2 : sigma(S)=sigma(T)} = 2^{2n} * int_0^1 prod_i cos^2(pi a_i theta) dtheta. (2) |cos(pi x)| <= exp(-2||x||^2), so |mu_hat(theta)| >= rho implies sum_i ||a_i theta||^2 <= (1/2) log(1/rho). Recalled (unverified constants): Chang's lemma: if A in G has density alpha and Spec_rho(A) = {r : |A_hat(r)| >= rho alpha}, then any dissociated subset of Spec_rho has size O(rho^{-2} log(1/alpha)). Burgin-Mao: sets A in Z^d with ||A||_{L^1(T^d)} = |A|^{o(1)}: a subset D Freiman-isomorphic to lattice points on a sphere has |D|/|A| polynomially small in |A|.
regime_exponents: [uncertain] The Fourier mass int prod cos^2 is exponentially small in n when the a_i are generic (about 2^{-n} up to poly) and large near a rank-d Bohr structure; sets with N_c about 2^{2n}/M (M= modulus/range) correspond to L^2 mass about 1/M. No concrete beta or D* thresholds in the sources; thresholds 0.311n, 0.5n, 0.661n are not addressed. Taking rho = 2^{-epsilon n} gives Bohr-set parameters of order epsilon n, i.e. the spectrum lives in a set of Bohr dimension up to about n and radius about sqrt(epsilon n).
proof_type_and_tools: [uncertain] Fourier/analytic: Parseval, Hausdorff-Young/Holder for L^4, Chang's lemma (entropy/Rudin-type inequality), Bohr sets and Bogolyubov-Ruzsa, large-spectrum covering; Burgin-Mao use Freiman-preserving projections, additive capacity and Bourgain-Demeter decoupling.
quantitative_loss: [uncertain] Chang's lemma has rho^{-2} log(1/alpha) dimension (polynomial in rho^{-1}) but with alpha exponentially small (alpha = 2^{-n(1-epsilon)} for bins) the dimension bound is of order n, i.e. no longer useful; Bohr set to GAP conversions lose exponentially in dimension (exp(O(d))) so they do not survive exponential energy.
worst_case_vs_average_case: [uncertain] The identity (1) is exact for every A (worst case). Structural conclusions via Chang/Bohr are worst case but weak at exponential energy; random a_i behave like a uniform measure with tiny L^2 mass except near rational frequencies.
coefficient_set: Natively {0,1}: each factor is (1+e(a_i theta))/2 and the cos^2 product handles pairs (S,T), equivalently {-1,0,1} relations weighted by 2^{|S cap T|}. {-1,0,1} and multiset versions correspond to cos or cos^2-type products with different multiplicities.
subset_size_regime: [uncertain] All subsets by default. Restriction to Theta(n)-slices requires a second Fourier variable (generating function in a counting variable z) or conditioning on size, adding a polynomial factor; disjoint pairs must be extracted from pairs (S,T) by cancelling S cap T, which weights by 2^{|S cap T|} and may dominate.
relevance_to_Nc: [uncertain] Gives the exact expression N(all pairs) = 2^{2n} int prod cos^2; upper-bounding it by exp(-4 sum ||a_i theta||^2) integrated reduces N_c to the volume of the Bohr set B(a, r) = {theta : sum ||a_i theta||^2 <= r}. Hence N_c is large iff the Bohr sets of the weights are large, a clean dual formulation for C1: hard instances have Bohr-volume about exp(-O(n)), and large N_c forces a Bohr set of volume 2^{-o(n)}.
relevance_to_Dstar: [uncertain] D* = min |T(S1,S2)|, the weight-n/8 sumset of two halves. Sumset size is bounded below via L^2/L^4 Fourier mass of the two half-distributions (Cauchy-Schwarz: |T| >= 1/ ||p||_2^2 for the convolution p). Small D* therefore forces a large L^2 mass, i.e. a heavy Bohr-set neighbourhood of 0 for the half-slice weights, giving a Fourier route to dichotomy 'D* small implies low-dimensional Bohr structure (GAP)'. Would need slice-restricted generating functions to apply.
applicability_gap: (i) Chang/Bohr control is for dense sets in a group of size M, whereas here densities are 2^{-Theta(n)} in range 2^{Theta(n)} (quasi-polynomial losses become exponential); (ii) Bohr set to GAP conversion is exponential in dimension; (iii) slices (size n/8) versus all subsets; (iv) disjointness weights 2^{|S cap T|}; (v) the 2026 Burgin-Mao paper treats Wiener norm of indicator functions of sets in Z^d, not the {0,1} subset-sum measure.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: Rank-d GAP with random generators (Bohr set of dimension d, large spectrum equals the annihilator lattice); arithmetic progressions (mu_hat concentrated near 0); random integers with huge modulus (flat spectrum); dissociated sets (|mu_hat| decays at every theta except 0).
dependency_chain: [uncertain] Fourier side of inverse_littlewood_offord (Halasz/Esseen); then Bohr to GAP, BSG/Freiman and PFR-type results to give structure; then lattice_relation_detection to certify the GAP; also underlies Steinerberger's proof of the distinct-subset-sums bound (distinct_subset_sums_extremal).
constructiveness: [uncertain] The Fourier mass is computable exactly for small n (numerical integration or FFT of the subset-sum histogram). Chang's lemma and Bohr-set arguments are existential; Bohr sets can be searched by lattice methods, but no efficient witness algorithm was verified.
lean_formalizable: [uncertain] Not realistically in a mathlib-free setting for Chang/Bohr; the identity (1) and the bound |cos(pi x)| <= exp(-2||x||^2) are elementary enough, but need real analysis (integrals) that the repo's Lean setup likely lacks. Working over Z/pZ with finite sums would make (1) a finite character-sum identity that is formalizable.
computational_check: [uncertain] No numerical experiments in the sources read. In the repo at n<=40: compute the exact collision count via the histogram of subset sums (equivalently identity (1) via FFT in Z/pZ for a prime p > n a_max) and compare to the Bohr-volume prediction for rank-1, rank-2 GAPs and random sets; feasible with scripts/analysis up to n about 30-40 using half lists.
next_experiment: [uncertain] For n=24, 32 and the repo's families, estimate the Bohr volume V(r) = Leb{theta : sum ||a_i theta||^2 <= r} by Monte Carlo and check whether log2(N_c) tracks n + log2 V(r*) for r* = O(1); this tests whether Bohr volume is a sufficient statistic for N_c.
open_issues: [uncertain] No source here handles exponentially small density; Chang's lemma statement and constants are recalled, not verified; 2609.26619 appears unrelated to {0,1} subset-sum measures (sets in Z^d with small Wiener norm), so its role in the project is unclear.
